transcript:
This is NPR News Now, the latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Corva Coleman, President Trump campaigned near Wichita,
Kansas yesterday for incumbent Republican Senator Roger Marshall.
In front of the rally crowd, Trump insulted Muslims and immigrants in his remarks while
Marshall insulted gays and lesbians.
Trump also announced a new program to give farmers one-time payments for diesel fuel costs.
This program is worth $8 billion.
Meanwhile, the president has recently struck a deal to suspend U.S. sanctions on sales
of Russian diesel.
He says this will help U.S. consumers.
And here's Emily Fang reports Trump's action will also help Russia.
He's had the Treasury Department lift sanctions on Russian diesel.
He's effectively suspended a sanctions bill.
He just signed into law that was named in honor of the late Senator Lindsey Graham.
He said yesterday he was willing to sit down with China's Xi Jinping and Russia's Vladimir
Putin to talk about the war on Ukraine, even if Ukraine's leader is not there.
And here's Emily Fang reporting.
California leaders say they will oppose the Trump administration's effort to fight alleged
illegal voting.
Yesterday, the Justice Department charged 28 green card holders with fraudulently registering
and voting in California.
And member station KQED, Tyke Hendricks, has more.
The charges are part of an escalating campaign, Operation Protect the Vote, to highlight
illegal voting by immigrants, which the president says is "rampant."
California Attorney General Rob Bonta says true voter fraud should be punished, but as
these arrests show, it's exceedingly rare.
28 out of 23 million registered voters in California is just a drop in the bucket numerically.
The charges come just after federal authorities sued California, over 20,000 registered voters
they allege are noncitizens.
A similar challenge in Nevada found zero noncitizens.
For NPR News, I'm Tyke Hendricks in San Francisco.
A former Columbia University graduate student is taking his case to the U.S. Supreme Court.
The Trump administration is trying to deport Mahmoud Khalil.
And Pierre's Kerry Johnson reports.
Mahmoud Khalil and his attorneys say he became a target of President Trump because of his
speech supporting Palestinian people in Gaza.
He says he broke no laws, and he's pursuing an appeal to the Supreme Court to make sure
immigrants can get a meaningful day in court.
The Third Circuit Court of Appeals ruled Khalil cannot raise arguments about free speech and
retaliation until his case plays out in the immigration courts, but that could take years.
A separate appeals court ruled the opposite way in a case involving a scholar at Georgetown.
Now the justices will consider whether to hear one or both cases this term.
The solicitor generals asked the Supreme Court to accept both cases and pair them.
Kerry Johnson, NPR News.
You're listening to NPR.
French officials imposed curfews overnight in parts of several cities, including Paris.
It's to stop unrest and some rioting that broke out last weekend.
Italy is deploying troops after riots in Milan.
There's been similar unrest in Albania.
A new study finds that people with attention deficit hyperactivity disorder had a higher
risk of dying from any cause compared with people without ADHD.
But NPR's Maria Godoy reports taking ADHD medication was linked to a lower risk of death.
Researchers analyzed the findings of 19 studies that included data from nearly 16 million
people with and without ADHD on three continents.
Some studies followed participants for more than 20 years.
They found that ADHD was linked to significantly higher risks of suicide and injury deaths,
as well as a moderately higher risk of dying from natural causes.
But they also found some evidence that this risk of mortality is lower among people who
take ADHD medication.
The researchers say the findings underscore the need for everyone who may have ADHD to
have access to accurate diagnoses and treatment.
The findings appear in the journal JAMA Network Open.
Maria Godoy and "PR News."
Wanna hear this podcast without sponsor breaks?

Trump announces $8 billion one-time diesel fuel payments for farmers
Trump administration suspends sanctions on Russian diesel sales, lifting Treasury restrictions
Trump says he's willing to meet Xi Jinping and Putin on Ukraine war without Ukraine's leader
Justice Department charges 28 green card holders with illegal voting in California
Federal authorities sue California over 20,000 alleged noncitizen registered voters
Mahmoud Khalil asks Supreme Court to hear deportation case over pro-Palestinian speech
French officials impose overnight curfews in several cities, including Paris, after unrest
Italy deploys troops after riots in Milan; similar unrest reported in Albania
Study finds ADHD linked to higher mortality, but ADHD medication associated with lower death risk
